text:
sam: noticing a spike in GPU evictions in ap-southeast warm-pool this morning, ~350 evicts over 30m. not correlated with user traffic increase.
hina: saw the alert. any correlation with the rack-level nic flaps last night?
sam: possibly. but distribution looks like small pods getting kicked when big-gang jobs land. packing imbalance.
liam: can you paste the scheduler-snap? I'm guessing affinity/anti-affine scoring is preferring a handful of racks.
sam: pasted a snippet from scheduler snapshot:
```
Top scoring nodes: rack-a-1 (score 95), rack-a-2 (score 92), rack-b-7 (score 12)
Pending tiny pods: 420
Gang jobs queued: 28 (large-gpu)
Warm pool available nodes: 6
```
liam: warm pool too small for bursty gang placement => scheduler picks best-fit racks and then small pods get preempted due to taint-based rebinds.
nina: are we running fractional gang preemptions? last rollout had the fractional-gang feature toggle on for ap-southeast.
sam: yes toggle=on. looking at recent rollout notes: "fractional-gang reduces coldstart overhead but can increase small-pod churn under rack skew".
hina: operator workaround: increase warm-pool size or relax taint for tiny pods for a few minutes when large gangs drain.
liam: we should also try a quick scheduler tweak: lower the nodeScoreWeight for rack affinity so pack spreads a little more across AZs. can we test on canary cluster?
sam: canary test scheduled. patch: set topologySpreadWeight -10 and fractional-gang backoff to 20s. will monitor.
scheduler-bot: [alert] evictions in ap-southeast warm-pool: 374 events in last 30m. avg latency spike 120ms. ticket created #INFRA-2741.
nina: note on cost: increasing warm-pool size will add ~0.9 GPU-hours per hour -> ~$1.1k/month if sustained. need approval if prolonged.
hina: good point. try scheduler tweak first, warm-pool scale only if evictions remain >100/30m after 1h.
liam: compiled a quick query to track preempted pods by cause:
```
count_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason~"Preempted|Evicted"}[30m])
```
sam: thanks. will post 30m and 1h charts. @oncall can you stand by for rollback instructions if pack spread regresses latency?
nina: @oncall FYI we may flip fractional-gang toggle if canary fails. rollback steps in runbook: runbook#scheduler->rollback-fractional-gang.
liam: post-canary: if spread improves and evictions drop <50/30m, we'll keep change and open RFC for fairness weighting.
sam: initial canary applied at 3741592680. will update with metrics in 10m.
nina: thx. also capturing node-level NIC error counters to correlate.
sam: update: at 3741592720 evictions dropped to 48 in last 10m on canary cluster. looks promising :thumbsup:
hina: great, hold for 20m then rollout to prod with 10% ramp.
liam: filing follow-up RFC: "scheduler: adaptive pack spread for mixed gang/tiny workloads". assign to eng-platform.
sam: closing thread for now, will post link to RFC and ticket when done.
